rules._comment: protect osiris-pg by its own container identity, not by its binary's exe path: the classifier checks a scope's OWN name (container_glob) against every rule BEFORE it ever looks at what's running inside, so an exe_glob rule for postgres can never win against a container_glob rule that matches every docker scope below. container_glob checks the container's own --name (ramsteind resolves it straight from dockerd's own records, no docker CLI needed) as well as the raw docker-<id>.scope name, so this matches as long as you ran the container with --name osiris-pg (or gave it that name in compose) -- the name survives a `docker compose` recreate that would otherwise rotate the ID out from under this rule. Placed BEFORE the cap-all rule below, since first match wins within container_glob's own pass.
protect the agent fleet -- every Claude Code session -- matched by its own binary path, since its process name is just a version string.
Chrome is expendable -- squeezed (never killed) only while the system is genuinely under pressure, released the instant it calms.

cap every OTHER docker container at 25% of total memory -- a standing ceiling regardless of system state, so no single container can quietly consume everything. Comes last: the container_glob rule above must win for osiris-pg specifically, or this catch-all claims it instead.
